transcript: I'm gonna be real honest, I have seen a lot of mid musicals with bad books lately and I was genuinely starting to wonder, am I being too critical? Have I just grown cynical in my old age? But then a musical like Benjamin Button comes along that is so perfectly constructed that it reminds you, oh yeah, great musical theatre does still exist. Because no exaggeration, I think this might be a perfect musical, and a rather ambitious one at that. Not only is it tackling this really abstract concept of man who ages backwards, but it is also attempting to tell his entire life story, which is famously really hard to do in a two and a half hour musical. And yet by the time you get to the end of the show, you really do feel like you have lived to this full life alongside him. And the story is told by a wonderful cast of actor musicians, many of whom are playing multiple roles in addition to their instrument of choice. They all work together as an ensemble so well, and yet they each get their own individual moments to shine. They also establish very early on that these actors are not necessarily playing roles that line up with their own age or gender, which I think is very smart because they're not using any makeup to age up Andrew Durand, who plays the main character, Benjamin Button. But because they've already built this high suspension Of disbelief that by the time Benjamin Button shows up, you just immediately accept that he is an old man. And I guess now is a good time to just praise Andrew Durand, He's going to win so many awards for this, and rightfully so. The way he is able to play this character throughout the many decades of his life is nothing short of brilliant. I was also really impressed with Kelsee Kimmel, who plays his love interest. Beautiful voice, great actress, and I think very much a star on the rise. And I haven't even talked about the score yet, which is just gorgeous. I've seen it described as once meets come from away, which I actually think is really accurate. And also two of my other favorite shows, So very much in good company. But if it wasn't clear yet, this show is obviously going to be a Broadway Ben must see. I think it might just be the best new musical in New York right now. And if it does end up coming to Broadway, I expect it to do very well at the Tonys.
